core_meaning.short_meaning: Radiant purity, brilliant white; celebrated female companion and poetess al-Khansa.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Tamadur (تُمَاضِر) is an illustrious Arabic feminine given name meaning 'radiant, luminous white', 'she who possesses pure clarity', or 'sweet-natured'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned personal name of Tamadur bint Amr ibn al-Harith, universally famous by her title al-Khansa'—the greatest poetess of classical Arabia who embraced Islam and whose four sons were martyred at al-Qadisiyyah.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Derived from al-maḍīr (pure white milk that is wholesome and sweet), signifying brightness, noble beauty, and untainted character.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root m-ḍ-r in Arabic signifies white radiance and sweet wholesomeness. As a historical name, Tamadur bint Amr was born into the noble Banu Sulaym tribe. She accepted Islam before the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, who admired her eloquence. At the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah, she sent her four sons into the fray with fiery exhortations; when all four fell as martyrs, she did not wail as in pre-Islamic times, but prostrated and thanked God for honoring her with their martyrdom.
